issues.summary: Silent money DOUBLE-COUNT when an upstream date is corrected on a line with NO invoice number. For blank-invoice lines greenBeanInvoices_ mints invoice_ref = '<supplierKey>/noinv-<dateLocal>' (orderapp.gs:460), so the date is part of the dedup identity — any date edit produces a NEW ref. The round-8 date-move self-heal keys on ref equality (orderapp.gs:879, inside the `if (snap)` branch), so it can never fire for these rows; and the rename detector's probe compares the BARE invoice-number part (orderapp.gs:865), which for a noinv ref is 'noinv-<date>' and therefore also differs, so no rename alert either. The old row survives, the new row appends, and nothing reconciles them. Verified empirically against the real code under the test mocks: (probe 3) a one-day correction Mon->Tue inside the SAME ISO week leaves Suppliers holding both 'slip_co/noinv-2026-06-22' $400 and 'slip_co/noinv-2026-06-23' $400, and because the new ref DOES mark its week affected, weeklySummarize actively rewrites Summary to $800 against a truth of $400 — an inflated figure served by doGet, with calendarEvents EMPTY. (probe 1) a cross-week correction gives Suppliers $500 against a truth of $250 and the OLD week is never resummarized, so the stale $250 also stays in Summary — two wrong weeks, zero alerts. (probe 5) the same fault double-counts a second supplier's blank-invoice row that moves day. Controls confirm the gap is specifically the date component, not noinv generally: the identical correction WITH an invoice number self-heals correctly to $250 (probe 2), and a noinv SUPPLIER rename is still detected and alerted (probe 4). Blank invoice numbers are a first-class case here — the code, docs and tests all handle them deliberately — and a hand-maintained 06_Stock_Intake sheet is precisely where a mistyped date gets fixed later. docs/schema.md's new 'A date correction upstream (same invoice, same total, moved date) self-heals' promises coverage that does not exist for this row shape. Fix: use the orphan signal rather than ref equality — any greenbean snapshot row whose storedDate falls inside greenBeanWindow_ but whose ref is absent from this pull's invoice set is a moved/renamed/deleted invoice, because the pull re-fetches the whole window by definition. That single rule subsumes the noinv date move, keeps the window bound round 7 added, and needs no bare-invoice-number matching.

A greenbean or shopify_orderapp trigger that STOPS FIRING is undetectable — the two new sources have no liveness watchdog at all. staleness.gs:30-36 removes both from STALENESS_SOURCES, justifying it as 'their failure detection is the orderapp fail-open counter/alert (orderapp.gs)'. That justification only covers runs that START and fail to finish: orderAppRunStart_ (orderapp.gs:113) increments the failcount from INSIDE the handler, so it can only ever fire when the handler actually runs. If the time trigger is deleted, disabled, or its authorization is revoked — the exact failure the staleness watchdog exists for — the failcount never increments, the heartbeat stamped by orderAppRunSuccess_ (orderapp.gs:142) simply stops advancing, and because stalenessRaiseAlerts_ only iterates STALENESS_SOURCES nothing ever reads that stale heartbeat. The feed goes permanently silent with no alert and no log, while Summary keeps serving the last figures it happened to have. This is a real regression in coverage versus the deleted shopify.gs, which WAS watched. The 96h threshold genuinely does not fit a 168h cadence (the stated reason for exemption is sound), so the fix is a per-source threshold rather than re-adding them at 96h — TODO.md already records that per-source thresholds are needed for the monthly 'recurring' source, and these two make it a second caller. Until then, both money feeds are unmonitored for the not-running case.

The date-move self-heal rewrites the date cell but leaves extracted_at stale. orderapp.gs:881 writes only column 1 (`suppSheet.getRange(snap.rowIndex, 1).setValue(invoice.date)`), whereas every other in-place correction in the hub updates the stamp alongside the value — upsertRows_ writes amountCol AND stampCol together (Code.gs:595-598), and appendSalesRow_ does the same (Code.gs:523-524). A row whose date was corrected therefore reports an extracted_at from the pull that first ingested it, so the one column an operator would use to answer 'when was this row last touched?' understates it, and a same-run total change is the only thing that refreshes it. One extra setValue on column 7 keeps the convention.
